what: This tracking stock represents Liberty Media's Formula One business and carries voting rights that the other class does not. Formula One owns the commercial rights to the world championship, selling media rights, race hosting fees and sponsorship.
customers: Broadcasters and streaming services, race promoters and host governments, sponsors, and fans buying tickets and hospitality.
money: fees paid by circuits and governments to host races
trackside and title sponsorship, hospitality and licensing
moat: There is only one Formula One world championship, and the teams, circuits and audience are contracted to it. No competitor can create a substitute.
risks: Race hosting fees depend on governments willing to subsidise events
Media rights are renegotiated in large blocks
The tracking stock structure makes ownership complicated
opportunities: Revenue grew about 23% last year and about 12% a year over three years
American audience growth has raised the value of US media and sponsorship rights
Adding races to the calendar adds hosting fees directly
watch: Media rights renewals and the number of races per season.
